cycleTime.interpretation: Time from a pull request being opened to being merged. In this pod the branch is built first and the PR is opened as the final step, so this measures review-and-merge latency — NOT how long the work took, and NOT comparable to DORA change lead time (commit to production).

epicLeadTime.interpretation: 83 epic(s) were documented after the work — their README was committed with the shipped status already set, so no elapsed time is measurable for them and they are excluded rather than counted as zero.

deployFrequency.proxyNote: Merged pull requests per week. No deploy log exists in this dataset, so this is a proxy for deploy frequency, not a measurement of it.

notInstrumented.label: Velocity (points per sprint)
notInstrumented.reason: Story points are not tracked in this dataset — there is nothing to sum.
notInstrumented.guardrail: Adopt a sizing convention, or accept throughput as the honest substitute.

notInstrumented.label: Cost per shipped point
notInstrumented.reason: Needs both story points and a token/spend ledger. Neither exists.
notInstrumented.guardrail: Instrument agent spend per epic; pair it with a sizing convention.

notInstrumented.label: Change failure rate
notInstrumented.reason: Zero true revert commits across the whole history. Fixes are folded forward, so there is no rollback signal to count — a computed rate here would read 0% and mean "not measured", not "no failures".
notInstrumented.guardrail: Record deploy outcomes and link incidents to the change that caused them.

notInstrumented.label: Failed-deployment recovery time
notInstrumented.reason: Requires paired incident start/resolve timestamps. No incident record exists.
notInstrumented.guardrail: An incident log with timestamps, linked to deploys.

notInstrumented.label: Throughput (stories per period)
notInstrumented.reason: No per-story ship event carries a timestamp. Epic-level throughput below is computed; story-level is not derivable without inventing a date.
notInstrumented.guardrail: Emit a ship event per story, or track story status transitions with dates.

benchmarks.label: DORA — Accelerate State of DevOps 2025
benchmarks.note: Elite performers: change lead time under one day; deployment frequency on demand. Cited, not republished.

benchmarks.label: LinearB Engineering Benchmarks 2026
benchmarks.note: Elite PR cycle time is measured in hours, not days. Cited, not republished.

benchmarks.label: DX Core 4
benchmarks.note: Speed, effectiveness, quality and impact are reported together — never speed alone.

rows.proxyNote: A reviewer-agent PR comment is a proxy for "automated review ran on this PR", not proof it caught anything.
rows.reason: Only 36 of 98 PRs carry an agent reviewer comment — under the 50% presence bar.

rows.proxyNote: A named CI check on a PR is a proxy for "quality was enforced automatically", not proof the check was strict.

evidence.detail: 83 of 98 PRs carry at least one CI check (e.g. "guards" on PR #107)

rows.criterion: Worktree isolation / parallel agents (overlapping branch lifetimes)
rows.proxyNote: Two PR lifetimes overlapping in time is a proxy for parallel agents on separate worktrees, not direct proof of worktree usage.

evidence.detail: PR #6 and PR #7 had overlapping open periods

rows.criterion: "Claude writes most of the code" (Co-Authored-By trailer ratio)
rows.proxyNote: A Co-Authored-By: Claude trailer ratio is a proxy for "the agent wrote most of the code", not proof.

evidence.detail: 87.2% of commits (733 of 841) carry a Claude co-author trailer

rows.criterion: Risk-tier merge discipline (PR-declared tier vs. merging identity)
rows.proxyNote: A HIGH-risk PR merged under a human identity is a proxy for merge discipline, not proof the risk tier itself was assessed correctly.

evidence.detail: 6 of 6 HIGH-risk PRs with a recorded merger were merged under a human identity

rows.criterion: Trusted self-verification loop (green-gate-before-merge rate, revert rate)
rows.proxyNote: A high green-before-merge rate and a low revert rate are proxies for "the team trusts the gate", not proof the gate itself is sufficient.
rows.reason: Green-before-merge rate 84.3% and/or revert rate 0.0% fall outside the trusted-loop bar (>=90% green, <=5% reverts).

rows.proxyNote: The presence of CLAUDE.md (and ways-of-work Skill provenance) is a proxy for "standards are encoded", not proof they are followed.
rows.reason: Neither CLAUDE.md nor AGENTS.md was found in the pushed extract.

notInstrumented.label: Auto-mode state
notInstrumented.reason: Whether auto mode is enabled is a local CLI/session setting. It is never written into a commit or a PR, so git history cannot answer it either way.
notInstrumented.guardrail: OpenTelemetry export of session state into the existing SIEM/observability stack (Step 1 guardrail).

notInstrumented.label: Live agent-concurrency count
notInstrumented.reason: How many agents are running at once is a point-in-time process fact. Git only records commits after the fact and never captures how many sessions were open concurrently.
notInstrumented.guardrail: Analytics to monitor team usage (Step 2 guardrail) — a live agent-concurrency dashboard.

notInstrumented.label: Token / cost per outcome
notInstrumented.reason: No token or spend ledger exists anywhere in git history. Cost-per-outcome needs a billing or usage-API join this dataset does not have — same gap pod-metrics.mjs names for cost-per-point.
notInstrumented.guardrail: Manage token use with model selection + the Analytics API (Step 3 guardrail).

notInstrumented.label: Automatic security review
notInstrumented.reason: A security-specific review pass is not distinguishable from an ordinary code-quality check in PR metadata unless it runs as its own named CI check — which this dataset does not carry.
notInstrumented.guardrail: Claude Security Review wired in as a named CI check (Step 2–3 guardrail/product).

notInstrumented.label: Proactive agent-kicks-off-agent monitor
notInstrumented.reason: Whether an agent proactively kicked off another agent, versus a human invoking it, is not recorded by git — the resulting commit and PR look identical either way.
notInstrumented.guardrail: Claude Tag monitoring a channel or data source and kicking off tasks proactively (Step 3 product) — instrument the trigger source.

notInstrumented.label: Agent sandboxing
notInstrumented.reason: Sandbox usage is a runtime execution-environment fact. It leaves no trace in git or PR metadata once the run completes.
notInstrumented.guardrail: Agent sandboxing (Step 3 product) — record sandbox usage per run.

caveats: Every number here is computed from this repository's own git and pull-request history. Nothing is estimated.
The comparison baseline is PUBLISHED BENCHMARKS, not an internal human-era baseline: this dataset has no human-majority era to compare against.
Metrics listed as "not instrumented" are absent because the data cannot support them — not because they are zero.
